entries.issuing_body: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
entries.title: Ninth Circuit holds sports event contracts are class III gaming under IGRA and that the Commodity Exchange Act does not preempt IGRA
entries.facts: In Blue Lake Rancheria v. Kalshi, Inc., No. 25-7504, decided September 16, 2026, a Ninth Circuit panel of Chief Judge Mary H. Murguia and Circuit Judges M. Margaret McKeown and Richard A. Paez, in an opinion by Judge McKeown, affirmed in part, reversed in part and remanded the district court's denial of a preliminary injunction sought by the Blue Lake Rancheria and the Chicken Ranch Rancheria of Me-Wuk Indians. The opinion states that the tribes are likely to succeed on their Indian Gaming Regulatory Act claims and that "The substance of the sports event contracts offered on Kalshi's DCM is sports gambling, regardless of whether Kalshi calls them swaps." It holds that such contracts are "located on Indian lands" when a user enters them from tribal territory even though the operator's infrastructure sits elsewhere, and that because the tribes' secretarial procedures incorporate tribal ordinances requiring tribal authorization for all class III gaming, unauthorized contracts violate those procedures. On the two federal statutes the opinion states: "Because IGRA and the CEA are not 'irreconcilable,' we must harmonize them... The CEA gives the Commission 'exclusive' jurisdiction over covered derivatives trading on designated contract markets. IGRA governs Class III gaming activity located on Indian lands." The opinion rejects the argument that the Unlawful Internet Gambling Enforcement Act displaces IGRA, and affirms dismissal of the tribes' Lanham Act claim, finding the statement that "Sports Betting [Is] Legal in all 50 States on Kalshi" to be unactionable opinion given unsettled legal questions about the products' legality. No injunction has issued: the panel remanded for the district court to consider the remaining preliminary-injunction factors. The underlying district court case is N.D. Cal. No. 3:25-cv-06162.

entries.issuing_body: U.S. House Committee on Financial Services
entries.title: House Financial Services Committee advances H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act, reported by a 28-21 vote
entries.facts: The House Financial Services Committee's public committee calendar lists a Full Committee "Markup of Various Measures" held September 16, 2026 at 10:00 AM in 2128 Rayburn House Office Building. The govinfo BILLSTATUS record for H.R. 8957 states that the bill is the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, that its official title is "To establish a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and other programs to ensure the transparent management of Bitcoin holdings of the Federal Government", that the sponsor is Rep. Nicholas J. Begich (R-AK) with 22 cosponsors including Rep. Jared Golden (D-ME-2), and that the bill was introduced and referred to the House Committee on Financial Services on May 21, 2026; that record listed no action later than the May 21 referral at the time it was retrieved. The Block, crypto.news, Cointelegraph, CryptoTimes, CryptoAdventure and Bloomingbit report that the committee approved the bill on September 16, 2026 by a vote of 28-21. As reported by crypto.news, under the bill bitcoin deposited into the reserve "would have to remain there for at least 20 years from enactment" and during that period "the assets could not be sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered or otherwise disposed of"; a study of acquisition strategies "does not authorize borrowing, new taxation, deficit spending or pledging federal assets as collateral to finance Bitcoin purchases"; and "Treasury would publish an annual report giving details on reserve holdings, transactions and control of private keys." As reported by The Block, the bill directs Treasury to establish and maintain a "secure Bitcoin storage facility" and to create a digital asset stockpile for other digital assets. The bill has not passed the House or the Senate.
